Research Lab 03

Control Theory

The mathematical backbone of autonomous systems. Control theory provides the rigorous framework for ensuring AI systems remain stable, predictable, and safe in real-world deployments.

Stability AnalysisFeedback SystemsState EstimationOptimal Control
Fundamental Concept

The Feedback Loop

At the heart of control theory is the closed-loop system: continuously measuring outputs and adjusting inputs to achieve desired behavior.

Reference
Desired state or goal (setpoint)
Error
Difference between desired and actual
Controller
Computes corrective action
Plant
The system being controlled
Output
Measured system response
Continuous Loop

The Classic Control Equation

u(t) = Kp·e(t) + Ki·∫e(τ)dτ + Kd·de(t)/dt

PID Controller: Proportional + Integral + Derivative

Core Principles

The Pillars of Control Theory

These fundamental concepts form the foundation for designing systems that behave predictably and safely.

Stability

Ensuring the system returns to equilibrium after disturbances—the foundation of reliable autonomous operation.

Controllability

The ability to drive the system from any state to any other state using available inputs within finite time.

Feedback

Using output measurements to adjust inputs, enabling self-correction and adaptation to changing conditions.

Observability

The capability to infer the complete internal state of a system from its outputs and inputs.

Control Strategies

Modern Control Approaches

From classical PID to learning-based methods, control engineers have developed diverse tools for different challenges.

PID Control

Proportional-Integral-Derivative: The workhorse of industrial control systems

Model Predictive Control

Optimizes future behavior using predictive models

Adaptive Control

Self-adjusting parameters in response to changing dynamics

Robust Control

Maintains performance despite uncertainty and disturbances

Optimal Control

Minimizes cost functions over trajectories

Neural Control

Learning-based controllers using neural networks

Applications

Control Theory Meets AI

Every autonomous system—from self-driving cars to robot surgeons—relies on control theory principles.

Autonomous Vehicles

Real-time control of steering, throttle, and brakes with safety guarantees

Robot Manipulation

Precise control of robotic arms for manufacturing and surgery

Drone Swarms

Coordinated control of multiple aerial vehicles

HVAC Systems

Energy-efficient building climate control

Power Grid Stability

Balancing supply and demand in electrical networks

AI Training

Controlling hyperparameters and training dynamics

Critical Infrastructure

Control Theory: The Silent Guardian of AI Safety

As AI systems take on more critical roles—from medical devices to power grids—control theory provides the mathematical guarantees we need. It's not enough for AI to be intelligent; it must be provably safe and stable.
